title: Chapter 13: Reason for Existence
content:
Chapter 13: Reason for Existence  
“Au revoir, you damn Pseudo-beast impostor.”
As I heard words I never imagined would come from Louise’s mouth, I pressed the foot pedal to dodge while manipulating the magic power converter switch with my hand.
I cut off the magic power flowing to the weapons and redirected it to the machine’s defense.
Magic power surged into the Thunderbolt’s armor, generating a force field—just as the left knee joint of the leg was shot through.
“Ugh!?”
With the impact, the Thunderbolt’s left leg vanished from the joint down.
I purged the left leg to lighten the machine, and through the camera eye, I saw Louise still aiming her large rifle.
The communication line was still open, and the conversation continued.
‘…Dodged from that position. Is that abnormal reaction speed thanks to the Pseudo-beast cells implanted in you? Or is it the ability of an enhanced soldier?’
Louise, who always carried a gentle aura, now had a terribly cold look in her eyes as she stood before me.
She fired a second shot while speaking, and I forced myself to dodge.
Her shooting accuracy was better than when we fought the Gijuu.
It seemed Louise had been hiding her true ability.
While narrowly avoiding the second shot, I asked her:
“...So it was you working behind the scenes, Louise.”
Surprised by my words, Louise’s eyebrow twitched slightly.
‘You noticed? For someone so naive, you’re surprisingly sharp.’
The third shot grazed the armor, but despite being protected by the force field, it pierced through and dissolved.
Compared to the beam-like attacks from a Second Class Gijuu, this had superior speed and power.
Above all, Louise’s aim was precise.
If I hadn’t dodged, the cockpit would have been shot through.
Feeling Louise’s murderous intent, I explained my reason.
“By chance. Before coming here, you insisted there was no subspace container on the Thunderbolt. But I never said the Thunderbolt didn’t have one.”
There had been many suspicious points until now, but the subspace container issue was decisive.
It was true that the Thunderbolt wasn’t equipped with one, but information about the experimental machine was classified.
I’d been concerned that she knew this, but I never expected her to attack me.
‘Hah, you panicked and failed. Maybe I got irritated seeing you obsess over Third Class? When we return, Belmer will scold me. Although... your murder will be a nice souvenir, so it’ll balance out!’
Beams kept firing in succession, and while dodging, my right arm was pierced and lost.
“Why you! Are you acting under someone’s orders?”
Looking back, it was Louise who guided us to the place where the attackers ambushed us.
Her suspicious behavior afterward, and her dealings with the attackers.
Louise had been deceiving me from the start.
Why was Louise targeting me? Under whose orders?
I tried to gather any information I could, but it seemed Louise noticed my intentions.
‘Don’t casually talk to me, you anomaly in the organization.’
Louise spoke in a harsh, cold voice, then unleashed all the feelings she held toward me.
‘Just talking to a Pseudo-beast impostor like you makes my skin crawl! I was kind to get details on the Prometheus Project, but I really hated it.’
Her words stabbed into my heart.
“Why go that far?”
‘Because it was necessary, obviously. Taking care of a clueless old man like you was a hassle!’
Louise’s emotions flared, and her attacks intensified.
‘Why do you think I approached you? Because you’re a nuisance to the organization.’
“The Prometheus Project’s upper management—”
‘Don’t you get it yet? Your existence is inconvenient for society.’
“I’m here to help militarize males—”
‘You still don’t realize you’re a dangerous existence?’
Louise looked at me with utter disbelief.
When I tried to put distance between us, she closed in, still aiming the large rifle.
Even while moving and shooting, her aim was accurate.
It was unbelievable that someone with such skill was stuck in Class 5, unable to transfer.
‘If you succeeded, do you know what would come next?’
I couldn’t answer Louise’s question.
I was too busy dodging, and honestly, I was scared to think about what lay ahead.
If the Prometheus Project succeeded, what awaited was—

‘They’d keep repeating risky surgeries under the pretense of securing manpower. How many men do you think would die? Thousands, tens of thousands of lives wasted trying to replicate your single success.’
“That’s…”
I faltered, and Louise’s eyes widened.
‘You don’t belong in this world. I was going to gather information and end it since you’d fail anyway, but you had to show off your useless talent!’
To Louise, I had become a threat.
“I don’t have any talent.”
When I denied it, she looked utterly exasperated.

‘Still don’t get it? You boarded a broken-down junk and survived, even defeating multiple Second Class alone. If this info got out, countless men dreaming of you would undergo dangerous surgeries. No one can imagine how many bodies would pile up. I can’t let you live and return as you are.’
The success of the Prometheus Project wasn’t necessarily beneficial to society.
Currently, the surgery success rate was low, and even if successful, it didn’t guarantee becoming a pilot.
Louise forced me to face the harsh reality that my existence would cause tragedy.
‘If you’d been killed by Gijuu, it would’ve been less trouble. But you had to show your strength, so now you’ll be killed by me.’
Maybe Louise’s purpose in sending me out was to have me die in action.
The fact that the kind Louise had been a lie shocked me mentally.
But I couldn’t end it here. I didn’t want it to end.
“Even so, I will live and make the project succeed. That is my reason for existence.”
Louise didn’t like my answer, showing a face full of fierce hatred.
She furrowed her brow and glared at me through the monitor.
‘Don’t act all resolute like a monster!’
Getting serious, Louise’s Battle Dress raised a beam cannon held by a large sub-arm.
Instead of a focused beam, it fired a scattered blast like a shotgun, attacking a wide area.
“Damn it!?”
Unable to dodge, the Thunderbolt was pierced by multiple beams, disabling flight and slamming into the sea.
Right after feeling the impact, Louise’s Battle Dress stomped on the Thunderbolt and aimed the large rifle at the cockpit.
‘Did you have a nice dream? Fighting Gijuu, getting close to someone as cute as me. Did you even hope we might date?’
Louise looked down at me with a faint smile.
Sure, fighting Gijuu was a nice dream.
But was the latter part really necessary?
If it were MC and hair styling, I might have been thrilled, but being betrayed as a friend hurt more.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/pa1NcFR.jpeg
I thought I had made friends at the academy...
“No, I wasn’t thinking about dating.”
I answered honestly, and Louise raised one eyebrow.
‘Not even showing regret at the last moment? You really feel like a doll.’
Watching Louise squeeze the trigger of the large rifle, I manipulated the magic power converter to inject magic into the chest.
I tried to generate a force field to protect the cockpit, but I doubted it could block Louise’s attack.
Just as the cockpit was about to be pierced by the beam, multiple water columns erupted around us.
The Thunderbolt rocked from the waves caused by the impact, and Louise hurriedly flew up to check the surroundings.
‘…Took too long.’
Louise muttered bitterly, looking up at something.
I checked the monitor footage and confirmed the situation had become even more desperate.
“A First Class…”
A huge Gijuu twice the size of the Thunderbolt appeared, with a hard-looking shell.
Its back was curved, with a fin made of the shell.
Sharp thorns protruded in various places, giving it an aggressive impression.
Distinctive were its thick, muscular arms and long tail.
Without the thick arms, it could look like a dinosaur.
It had six eyes on its head—a species classified as First Class called “Baoga.”
Green glowing orbs resembling eyeballs were nestled in the gaps of its shell, and when they moved, it prepared to fire beam-like attacks.
‘This is bad!?’
Louise no longer had the luxury to deal with me and distanced herself from the Thunderbolt, beginning evasive maneuvers.
Inside the immobile machine, I heard an alert signaling the Gijuu’s strong reaction.
“The force field strength is way beyond Second Class.”
I measured the magic power, and even just the force field covering the surface was orders of magnitude stronger than Second Class.
Few soldiers survived encounters with First Class Gijuu on the battlefield.
Most who lived were lucky, like me.
To infantry, encountering one meant death—a grim reaper.
But apparently, it was the same for Louise.
It must be difficult to face a First Class with a training machine like the Battle Dress.
From the open communication line, I heard Louise’s troubled voice.
When Baoga fired beam-like attacks from the green glowing orbs on its body, it unleashed high-power energy with speed and density unlike Second Class.
The beams slowly changed direction, chasing Louise.
‘I can’t deal with a First Class in a training machine!’
Though the homing ability didn’t seem high, being chased by a high-output beam was terrifying.
Louise fired the sub-arm beam cannon while dodging but couldn’t penetrate Baoga’s force field.
‘Ridiculous defense. I really don’t want to face this kind.’
Baoga’s defining trait was its toughness.
Not only was its force field strong, but its shell was extremely hard.
Baoga itself was a power type.
Just swinging its massive arms crushed most things.
We were shown footage of Baoga rampaging in urban areas during training, easily toppling buildings.
It grabbed and crushed resisting tanks with its hands.
Even tanks were toys before Baoga.
Watching the scene, I pondered how to survive here.
Fortunately, Baoga was targeting Louise and hadn’t noticed me.
Inside the cockpit, I searched for a way to survive.
“Abandon the machine and escape… no, there are Third Class nearby. If I leave, I’ll be their prey.”
Even staying in the cockpit, Baoga would eventually notice me.
While thinking, the radar caught a friendly unit approaching fast.
I turned the camera eye toward the direction.
“From above?”
Approaching from the sky was a Valkyrie wearing a white and red Valkyrie Dress.
It was much larger and differently designed than Louise’s.
It seemed to have firearms on its sub-arms but showed no sign of using them, only speeding closer.
“Are they planning to ram?”
I shouted, not knowing who it was, and a communication line opened between us.
‘Just watch quietly.’
The suddenly appeared ally charged straight at Baoga.
Instead of sub-arms, it held small star-shaped shields in its hands.
Baoga reacted strongly to the new ally, ignoring Louise and turning its body with a roar.
Though it had no mouth, a roar echoed around, and more beam-like attacks than before were fired at the ally.
Baoga seemed instinctively afraid of the newcomer.
It repeatedly fired excessive beam attacks.
The ally dodged the beams without slowing, closing in on Baoga and preparing its weapon.
A blade of light emerged from the small shield, and as it passed Baoga, it swung it.
The light blade extended and fanned out.
The ally passed Baoga by several hundred meters, then slowed down while turning back.
‘Here comes the hero, huh?’
Baoga stopped moving, but lines appeared on its hard shell.
Its fluids leaked out, and its neck and upper body slid down and fell.
“I can’t believe it took only two swings to take down a First Class…”
I couldn’t believe what I saw.
Wide-eyed, the ally approached and spoke to me.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/oh2kWeY.jpeg
‘That was close. Also, consider this a favor—I expect you to return it properly later.’
The person on the monitor was someone I knew.
“...Lieutenant Hayase.”
‘Your machine’s a wreck, but you look fine. Come on, let’s go.’
Maya Hayase—the ace of Boots Cat—had come to rescue us.
While I was stunned, Louise approached Lieutenant Hayase.
‘Thank you so much, Maya. I thought I was going to die.’
Louise had already returned to her usual fake smile, a completely different person from before.
Lieutenant Hayase, who was met with such a friendly smile, aimed the large-caliber rifle held on her sub-arm at Louise.
The muzzle was pointed, ammo loaded, ready to fire at any moment—proof she was wary of Louise.
‘If you come any closer, I’ll shoot.’
Unlike her earlier conversation with me, Lieutenant Hayase spoke coldly.
Louise seemed quite flustered, her gaze wandering.
‘Huh? What? Did I do something to make you mad?’
‘How long are you going to keep pretending to be someone else? You’re the one who shot through this machine’s arm, right?’
Lieutenant Hayase glanced at the Thunderbolt’s right arm, pierced by Louise.
Louise desperately started making excuses.
‘N-no! That was the Gijuu!’
To me, it sounded like a transparent lie.
“Lieutenant Hayase, I—”
As I tried to explain, Lieutenant Hayase mounted a blade-like weapon on her back and held up her palm, signaling me to be silent.
Her gaze stayed fixed on Louise, not looking away—clearly cautious.
‘I already understand most of it, so you don’t need to say anything. And Louise—stop pretending to be a cat. Your fake sweet voice has been annoying since middle school.’
Harsh words, but knowing Louise’s true nature, I felt it was justified.
Louise seemed to give up hiding and revealed her true self before Lieutenant Hayase.
‘You’ve always been sharp, haven’t you?’
Louise smirked faintly, and Lieutenant Hayase said without changing expression:
‘That face suits you much better.’
‘...Thank you, Maya. By the way, can you hand him over?’
Louise pointed at me, and Lieutenant Hayase fired the large-caliber rifle.
The left sub-arm of the Battle Dress was blown off, and Louise’s eyes widened.
‘I told you not to move. Answer only my questions.’
Louise fell silent, and Lieutenant Hayase began questioning.

‘You were awfully reckless. I was shocked when you attacked inside the academy, but did you really try to assassinate the target during the mission? That’s laughably poor. You hid your true self so thoroughly, then acted at such a timing.’
Indeed, Louise’s actions were too rash.
Despite hiding her true nature and blending in, there was an undeniable sense of incongruity.
She should have prepared carefully, so what was the purpose of the academy attack and this timing?
Louise calmly began explaining to Lieutenant Hayase.
‘…You noticed too, right? If he lives and the project somehow succeeds, do you know what awaits? Militarizing men isn’t as gentle as it sounds.’
Lieutenant Hayase remained silent, seemingly uninterested in listening.
Louise took this as permission and pointed out the Prometheus Project’s problems, just as she did with me.

‘Principal Kase accepted it half-jokingly, but if their plan succeeds, who do you think loses out? Men with no choice but to undergo dangerous surgeries for militarization. Is that a good thing? Wouldn’t killing the test subjects here and stopping the project be better for society?’
If the Prometheus Project succeeded, the organization would likely recruit volunteers from former soldiers who lost limbs to prepare pilots.
Hopefully, they’d find a revolutionary method to drastically increase surgery success rates, but as things stand, the surgeries would be as risky as mine or only slightly better.
Many casualties would surely follow.
Lieutenant Hayase listened to Louise’s words and sneered.
‘You parade around with grand reasons, but your words are shallow. Be honest… you’re just scared that men gaining power will take away yours.’
Lieutenant Hayase’s words hit the mark, and Louise’s expression changed drastically.
‘You ignorant mole of a student, getting cocky!’
As Louise tried to raise her weapon, Lieutenant Hayase closed the distance instantly.
She cut the large rifle with the blade she used earlier.
Lieutenant Hayase’s left sub-arm destroyed Louise’s remaining sub-arm with a gatling gun, rendering it useless.
She quickly neutralized Louise, who had tormented me.
Though Louise lost her weapons, she swiftly drew a hidden blade from behind her waist.
Their blades clashed, and they resumed their conversation.
Being called a mole seemed to narrow down Louise’s affiliation a bit.
‘Calling our academy a mole means you’re working for another academy, right? You’ve been undercover for years.’
‘Don’t let the reclusive Third Academy meddle in central politics now!’
‘Say that to the principal if you want.’
Their blades sparked and clashed fiercely.
But to me, Lieutenant Hayase seemed to be holding back.
Louise seemed to sense this and looked irritated.
‘None of this concerns you! You don’t care if that guy dies!’
Lieutenant Hayase had no reason to protect me.
Yet, she smiled broadly.
‘—I can’t hate someone who desperately struggles and finally grabs a chance. Honestly, I got mad at you for pretending and deceiving, so I interfered.’
“You just didn’t like him, so you got in the way,” Louise said, her face twisted with anger.
‘You! Just by living, you’re a nuisance to everyone!’
Louise struck a sharp blow, but Lieutenant Hayase easily deflected it and forced her arms up.
With Louise’s abdomen exposed, she kicked her away.
“Ugh…”
Louise was sent flying into the sea, and Lieutenant Hayase looked down at her.
‘I don’t care about what you say.’
Louise, unable to get up, looked up and retorted.
‘If I weren’t in a training machine, I would have won.’
Lieutenant Hayase smiled.
‘That’s what a cat pretending to be innocent says.’
Their fight ended abruptly.
Then, black-clad Valkyries appeared around us.
They surrounded us, weapons drawn, with “SVAT” written in white on their Battle Dresses.
“Who are they?”
Lieutenant Hayase answered my question.
‘They’re called Sabbat. A special unit handling problems like this.’
The black-clad Valkyries approached Louise, weapons ready, and began restraining her.
‘Lieutenant Louise Durand, you will come with us.’
Louise, restrained, floated up and obediently followed the Sabbat members.
She glanced back at me once.
‘Ah, I missed killing you. Someone interfered.’
Louise no longer pretended, but her smile remained—a wild, emotion-filled grin unlike before.
Lieutenant Hayase spat toward her back.
‘I’ll catch your comrades who attacked us soon.’
Louise laughed after a few seconds.
‘You’re really naive. Try to catch us if you can. I guarantee it’s impossible as things stand.’
The Sabbat members then surrounded us.
‘We’ll hear your story, so both of you come with us.’
“...Understood.”
I accepted, but Lieutenant Hayase looked displeased.
‘Isn’t it strange to be interrogated when I called you?’
Lieutenant Hayase showed a defiant attitude, and the Sabbat members, though confused, escorted us away.
